prompts.description: Rename onboarding entry paths: Quick Start to Estimate, InBody path to Precise (InBody)
prompts.prompt: In components/onboarding.tsx, locate the entry screen where the user chooses between the two onboarding paths (Quick Estimate / quick start vs InBody / precise). Rename the user-facing labels ONLY: the quick-estimate path button/card title becomes "Estimate" and the precise path becomes "Precise (InBody)". Update any subtitle/description copy so it no longer claims the Estimate path is faster or has fewer fields — instead describe it as "Estimate body composition from your body type" for Estimate and "Enter exact InBody measurements" for Precise (InBody). If Korean strings exist (language === 'ko'), update them too: "추정" and "정밀 (InBody)" with matching descriptions. Do NOT change any logic, field order, state, or the applyQuickEstimate flow — labels and description copy only. Verify: npm run build passes and the onboarding entry screen shows the new names.

prompts.description: Make per-meal status pill look tappable in Daily View (icon + button styling)
prompts.prompt: Building on the existing meal status pill in components/daily-view.tsx (the pill that cycles planned/eaten/skipped/cheat on each meal card). Make it visually obvious the pill is interactive WITHOUT changing its click/cycle logic. Changes: (a) add a small Lucide icon inside the pill indicating it cycles — use the RotateCw icon (size 12) placed left of the status label; (b) style the pill as a button: add subtle border, rounded-full, px-2.5 py-1, cursor-pointer, and a hover state (slightly darker bg); (c) add an active/press feedback via active:scale-95 transition-transform. Keep the existing per-status color scheme intact. Do NOT change the status cycling handler, the Meal type, or any Zustand logic. Verify: npm run build passes and tapping the pill still cycles status, now with visible button affordance + press animation.

prompts.description: Increase visibility of ingredient-selection warning text in onboarding
prompts.prompt: In components/onboarding.tsx, locate the warning shown when the user has selected fewer than the required ingredients (text similar to "Select at least X proteins, Y carb, and Z fat to continue"). Increase its visibility: wrap it in a styled alert container with bg #FEF2F2, border 1px #DC2626, rounded-md, padding 10px 14px, text color #B91C1C, font-weight 600, and a Lucide AlertCircle icon (size 16, color #DC2626) before the text. Apply the same alert styling pattern to any other inline validation warning in onboarding.tsx so warnings are consistent. Do NOT change the validation logic or the minimum-selection rules — styling only. Verify: npm run build passes and the warning is clearly visible against the background.

prompts.description: Trigger AI ingredient lookup on Enter key in onboarding ingredient search
prompts.prompt: In components/onboarding.tsx, locate the ingredient search input where fetchIngredientViaClaude is called when a searched ingredient is not in the catalog (currently triggered by a button). Add an onKeyDown handler to that search input so pressing Enter triggers the same AI lookup action as the existing button. Guard against empty/whitespace-only input (do nothing if trimmed value is empty) and prevent default form submission. Do NOT remove the existing button and do NOT change fetchIngredientViaClaude itself — only wire the Enter key to the existing handler. Verify: npm run build passes and pressing Enter in the ingredient search field triggers the AI lookup.

prompts.description: Add a Go-to-top floating button on long-scroll screens (Settings + Grocery List)
prompts.prompt: Create a reusable component components/scroll-to-top.tsx: a fixed-position floating button (bottom-right, bottom-20 right-4, z-40) that appears only after the user scrolls down more than 400px and smooth-scrolls to top on click. Use a Lucide ArrowUp icon (size 20), circular button (h-10 w-10 rounded-full), bg #26603F, text white, shadow-lg, hover darkens slightly. Track scroll position with a useEffect scroll listener and local useState (cleanup listener on unmount). It must not overlap existing FABs — if a bottom-right FAB already exists on a screen, position this above it. Then mount <ScrollToTop /> in the two longest-scroll screens: components/settings-screen.tsx and components/grocery-list.tsx. Do NOT add it to onboarding or daily-view. Verify: npm run build passes; scrolling down past 400px on Settings or Grocery List reveals the button, and clicking it scrolls to top.
